episodes.157785: During the late evening hours of June 12th, a series of thunderstorms slowly moved through central Indiana from the north.  An outflow boundary in eastern Marion county led to additional thunderstorm growth north of Indianapolis that eventually would bring damaging winds and large hail to portions of Indianapolis and western Hancock County. Slow storm motions and backbuilding led to some areas to receive up to 3 inches of rain which caused isolated flash flooding.  Over 20,000 power outages were caused by the thunderstorms with some noted to be from lightning strikes and others from tree and power pole damage.
episodes.157794: A cold front brought isolated late afternoon and evening severe storms that produced large hail, heavy rain and frequent lightning as well as isolated reports of damaging wind gusts.  The most severe weather occurred in Ovid in south central Michigan where baseball sized hail was reported in addition to several downed trees and power lines.

episodes.157823: A small MCS crossed the Laurel Highlands during the late morning hours of June 13, 2021, with wind damage being reported in Somerset County. Later in the day, additional showers and storms developed in the very warm and humid airmass over central Pennsylvania, ahead of an approaching cold front. These late-day storms produced sporadic wind damage and hail reports.
episodes.157828: Showers and thunderstorms occurred along a cold front moving through the Ohio Valley during the afternoon hours. Some of the storms produced damaging winds and locally heavy rainfall.

episodes.157846: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed during the mid-afternoon hours across Northcentral Louisiana on June 13th, near a weak surface trough extending from Southeast Oklahoma, extreme Southwest Arkansas, and North Louisiana. Compressional warming and low level moisture pooling near this boundary resulted in a very unstable air mass developing across much of the region, with a weak upper level disturbance sliding southwest across North Louisiana and East Texas during the afternoon and evening contributing to increasing large scale ascent. As a result, one of these storms became severe over Eastern Union Parish Louisiana, producing damaging winds which downed a large tree on a home west of Sterlington. These storms continued to redevelop and shift west-southwest across North Louisiana through the evening and into East Texas after midnight.
episodes.157865: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a weak cold front as it moved southeast across the lower Ohio Valley. The environment was very moist and unstable, with dew points in the lower to mid 70's. Dry air in the mid levels of the atmosphere promoted locally damaging downdraft winds.

episodes.157905: With an area of high pressure centered over southwest New Mexico, temperatures soared across northern and central portions of the state on June 12, 2021. Dry weather prevailed for most areas west of the Rio Grande Valley, but a cold front was responsible for drastically different weather conditions across the east. The cold front moved through eastern New Mexico late on June 11th and helped to replenish low-level moisture and provide an highly unstable and sheared environment. The result was a round of strong to severe thunderstorms that developed first over the northern high terrain and then moved east to southeast onto the plains. The strongest thunderstorm was a supercell near Las Vegas that produced very large hail up to three inches in diameter as well as a tornado. While the hail did some damage in the form of broken windshields, the tornado was over open country. As the thunderstorms marched towards the Texas border, the severe weather threat shifted to primarily a wind threat, and wind gusts exceeding 60 mph were recorded at several locations.
episodes.157922: A severe thunderstorm produced straight-line winds in Cocoa, which resulted in damage to two homes, in addition to tree damage.
episodes.157923: Numerous afternoon thunderstorms that moved across Volusia and Brevard County produced several strong wind gusts.
episodes.157925: A cold front was pushing across eastern KY during the afternoon and evening hours on June 13th. Ahead of this front, a warm and moist airmass provided the perfect environment for thunderstorms to develop. These thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts and small hail, with numerous reports of trees being blown down as they rolled through.

episodes.158103: Severe thunderstorms moved across portions of Goshen and Laramie Counties producing hail stones up to the size of golf balls.
episodes.158247: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front during the evening hours across north-central, northeast, and east-central Wisconsin.  The strongest storms produced isolated wind damage and small hail.

episodes.158456: A slow moving thunderstorm became severe over central portions of Weston County, producing large hail near Osage.
episodes.158465: Several trees were blown down by wind gusts from a line of thunderstorms that tracked south across Rhea, Bradley, and Hamilton counties.
episodes.158473: A slow-moving cold front interacted with a highly unstable but weakly sheared environment to trigger scattered strong to severe thunderstorms across east-central Illinois during the late afternoon and early evening of June 12th.  Some of the storms produced wind gusts of around 60mph and caused minor wind damage.
episodes.158611: A southward propagating cold front served as a focal point to spark severe thunderstorms across southwest Virginia during the afternoon and evening|of June 13th.
episodes.158612: A southward propagating cold front served as the focus for the development of severe thunderstorms that produced damaging winds on the afternoon of June 13th.
episodes.158766: A lingering front near the I-10 corridor combined with an upper level trough aloft. These features combined with the sea breezes over a moist and unstable airmass with weak steering flow produced flooding rainfall over parts of Jacksonville and a few pulse severe storms that had wet downbursts.
episodes.158938: An advancing cold front, along with shortwave support, created the chance for thunderstorms across the region. Sufficient shear (40kts in the 0-6km layer), moderate to high instability (1500-2000 J/kg of CAPE), and dry mid-level air resulted in damaging winds and hail.
episodes.158940: An advancing cold front, along with shortwave support, created the chance for thunderstorms across the region. Flash flooding occurred, mostly south of Pittsburgh, with training storms.

episodes.159036: A cold front combined with an unstable atmosphere, plenty of moisture, and a light flow aloft to cause isolated flooding instances over the Potomac Highlands of Virginia as well as central Virginia.
episodes.159177: A strong cold front in accordance with a passing low pressure system pressed into West Virginia on the evening of June 13th. Strong to severe thunderstorms accompanied the front, resulting in multiple instances of downed trees and power lines due to damaging wind gusts. Due to the combination of heavy downpours and multiple storms passing over the area that day, several counties observed flash flooding. The most notable events occurred in Gilmer County, where a large shed on a golf course was swept away by the rushing high water, and Pocahontas County, where a swift water rescue was conducted in the town of Frost.
episodes.159218: A cold front sweeping through the Ohio Valley on the evening of June 13th prompted a few strong thunderstorms to develop over southeast Ohio. This resulted in downed trees and broken large branches in Jackson and Washington Counties.
episodes.159219: A cold front associated with a low pressure system crossed through eastern Kentucky on the evening of June 13th. Damaging wind gusts occurred in several severe thunderstorms that day, which resulted in a few instances of downed trees across Greenup County. Heavy downpours associated with these storms also resulted in a washed out road in Greenup County.
episodes.159290: An upper disturbance moving across the area produced a strong thunderstorm in Munising on the evening of the 13th.
episodes.159310: An upper-level trough over the region along with a weak cold front to produce isolated severe thunderstorms over north and central Georgia.
episodes.159367: A weak upper level disturbance moved along the northern side of an upper level ridge centered across the Desert Southwest generating thunderstorms over the mountains of Colorado and New Mexico. These storms slowly moved east into the Panhandles and encountered an environment with weak to moderate wind shear but extreme instability and high moisture which allowed these storms to thrive and increase in severity and organization as they tracked east. The main impact from the storms were from damaging winds as they crossed out of New Mexico and Colorado into the Panhandles, but some hail was also reported. The most significant damage occurred with a storm that strongly bowed as it moved southeast across Cimarron County Oklahoma. This storm produced wind speeds likely around 90 mph in some locations based on damage and were measured just shy of 80 mph near Boise City, OK at a mesonet site. The storm produced widespread wind damage from Kenton to Boise city and southeast to Griggs, OK. Widespread damage to trees and powerlines occurred and isolated significant roof damage occurred as well, including the Boise City High School auditorium, which lost part of it's roof completely. Fifty-five power poles were reported damaged across Cimarron County with around 1600 customers without power during the peak outage after the storms. Power was out until well into the afternoon hours on Sunday for some locations. This storm continued to grow upscale and eventually merged across the northwestern Texas Panhandle with another broken line of storms that had crossed the New Mexico border near I-40, also producing severe wind gusts as they entered the Texas Panhandle. This storm complex tracked east-southeast and continued to produce severe wind gusts and heavy rainfall, especially across the northern and central Texas Panhandle. The storms finally weakened early Sunday morning as instability decreased.

episodes.159493: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail across parts of Adams, Arapahoe, Denver, and Weld counties.  The hail ranged in size from quarter to golfball size.  The hail did cause some damage to vehicles at Cherry Creek State Park.  Thunderstorm wind gusts up to 59 mph were observed in Morgan and Logan counties.

episodes.159735: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon hours on June 12th. Some storms became severe with several reports of wind damage, hail, and flash flooding.
episodes.159756: Isolated severe storms developed over central Lower Michigan on the afternoon and evening of June 12, 2021, including a long-lived supercell. This storm produced significant hail - some up to baseball-sized in Ovid, Michigan (Clinton County) - and a few instances of wind damage as it tracked from the Mt. Pleasant area all the way to Ann Arbor before dissipating in the late evening. Other clusters of storms developed in the evening over northern and central Lower Michigan, one of which tracked across Midland and Bay Counties and resulted in localized damaging wind gusts.
episodes.159816: Slow-moving thunderstorms trained across southern Highland County, forming in an environment of CAPE exceeding 2,500 J/Kg and Precipitable Water of around 1.5 inches.  The storms produced 2.5 to 4 inches of rainfall amounts over a 2 to 3-hour period, with rainfall rates at times reaching 5 to 6 inches per hour.  Steep terrain in the Back Creek basin aided in creating efficient runoff to cause the stream gauge at Back Creek at Sunrise to rise to 10.01 feet, exceeding Moderate Flood Stage set at 10 feet.  This is the highest this gauge has risen since 2008.  FLASH estimated that rainfall just upstream from the stream gauge was over 3 times greater than 1-hour Flash Flood Guidance.  CREST Unit Streamflow was estimating over 1,000 cfs per square mile, whiile CREST 1-hour Average Return Interval estimates put this rainfall at well over a 200-year event.
episodes.159842: A couple rounds of thunderstorms developed in central and north central South Dakota, one around noon and another around midnight, and produced severe wind and hail.
episodes.160002: A mesoscale convective system coming from portions of the region northwest of the area, raced southeast across the local area. This feature produced mostly damaging wind impacts over both land and water areas.

episodes.160043: The upper air pattern transitioned from west to northwest flow across Alabama during this time period.  Deep moisture with PWAT's above 1.8 inches combined with increasing mid level lapse rates to create favorbale conditions for heavy rainfall and strong thunderstorm winds.
episodes.160134: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with a few strong thunderstorms producing wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.160145: Central Kentucky sat under the leading edge of an upper ridge during a period of typical summer weather.  Temperatures rose during the day creating strong instability in the atmosphere that caused showers and thunderstorms to breakout. As rain filled downdrafts initiated outflow boundaries, the outflow boundaries initiated more storms. This happened daily before a weak cold front pushed drier air into the region. Several counties in central Kentucky received isolated wind damage during this three day stretch. Scott County had flooding issues on June 13th.
episodes.160222: Strong thunderstorms moved across the marine area and produced gusty winds.
episodes.160315: Impressive storms developed on the converging lake breeze over the Niagara Peninsula in Ontario. These cells slowly tracked eastward toward the Niagara River. Each cell rapidly fell apart as it moved into the United States, however one cell managed to drop nickel sized hail near the Niagara River.
episodes.160613: Daytime heating led to large amounts of instability and a few strong to severe storms across West Tennessee with some hail and damaging winds during the afternoon and evening on June 12, 2021.
episodes.160614: Daytime heating led to large amounts of instability and a few strong to severe storms across East Arkansas with some hail and damaging winds during the afternoon of June 12, 2021.
episodes.160624: Convective cloud lines developed within broad cyclonic lower tropospheric flow, resulting in several waterspouts developing in Florida Bay north of the Lower Keys.
episodes.161803: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed over northern portions of Mississippi during the afternoon of June 13th and quickly spread south and west across the state. Several significant events of wind damage occurred as these storms spread across the region, with some houses impacted by high wind and fallen trees.

A roughly 7 mile by 4 mile swath of damaging winds occurred in the Okatibbee Lake area, with estimated peak gusts of 75-85 mph. Initial wind gusts of 60-70 mph blew down scattered trees along MS Highway 495, Pine Springs Road, and Okatibbee Creek Park. Winds likely spread out and accelerated as they surged southwest across the open waters of the lake. Multiple focused swaths of extensive wind damage occurred along Center Hill Martin Road, Hamrick Road, and Okatibbee Dam Road. Extensive tree damage was also noted at Twitley Branch Campground, Collinsville Park, and along the Okatibbee dam and West Bank park. Numerous hardwood and softwood trees were uprooted along the immediate western shore of the lake. As the surging winds spread further west, they quickly weakened to 60-70 mph with only a few scattered trees blown down along MS Highway 19.
